title: The Leopard Seal Hunts Penguins, Yet Half Its Meals Are Krill
subject: leopard seal

scenes.text: Penguins fear this seal. Yet half its meals are tiny krill.
It's the leopard seal. A big female reaches about 3.6 meters and 500 kilograms.
It waits by Adelie penguin colonies and grabs birds that slip into the water.
It grips a penguin and shakes it hard at the surface until the skin tears away.
But its back teeth are lobed like a sieve, so it can strain krill from the water.
It's the only seal that regularly kills warm-blooded prey, and it still lives on krill.

description:
Leopard seals are the only seals known to regularly hunt warm-blooded prey, including penguins and other seals.
Yet krill makes up almost half of their diet, which they strain out with lobed back teeth.
Which side of this seal scares you more?
first_comment: Would you rather meet a leopard seal on the ice or in the water?
